Josh Bilicki to Enter 2027 Daytona 500 in Protection Technologies Car for Garage 66

by Speedway Digest Staff
August 31, 2026
Reading Time: 3 mins read
0

Garage 66 Image

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 3:26
Instaread

Garage 66 is thrilled to announce that Josh Bilicki is set for an entry into the 69th Daytona 500, driving the No. 66 Protection Technologies NASCAR Cup Series car next February at Daytona International Speedway.

SportsNews

Protection Technologies designs, installs, and commissions complete low-voltage security systems for many types of clients, including general contractors, property managers, commercial real estate, government and municipal facilities, and professional sports venues. They have active partnerships with major sports franchises in the NFL, NBA, NHL, and MLS, and this Daytona 500 entry adds motorsports to their growing portfolio for the first time.

“In this business, I’ve gotten to do some pretty remarkable things and work with clients at the highest levels of sports and entertainment,” said Mike Singer, President of Protection Technologies. “But putting Protection Technologies on a Daytona 500 car? This tops the list. February can’t come fast enough.”

The partnership between Garage 66 and Protection Technologies kicked off on Monday night at Ole Red, the live music venue, restaurant, and country bar on International Drive in Orlando, Florida, with Josh and Mike unveiling the paint scheme together to be run during Speedweeks 2027.

For Bilicki, the Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin native is gearing up for his second entry into the Great American Race, having earned a Top 25 finish in his first start. The 31- year-old has more than 270 starts across the three NASCAR national divisions, including more than 100 in the premier series. His best NASCAR Cup Series finish to date also came at Daytona, when he drove to a Top 10 result in the 2021 Coke Zero Sugar 400.

SportsNews

“I’m incredibly excited to welcome Protection Technologies to Garage 66 as we attempt next year’s Daytona 500,” said Bilicki. “They’ve built a great reputation in their industry and I’m proud to have the opportunity to represent their brand on the biggest stage in NASCAR. I was fortunate enough to compete in the Daytona 500 in

2021, but haven’t had the opportunity to return since, so this means a lot to me. I’m

grateful to Protection Technologies, Carl Long, and Garage 66 for giving me the

opportunity!”

Garage 66 co-owner Carl Long is ecstatic about releasing 2027 news this early in the calendar and has a positive outlook on the prospects for his organization.

“I am excited to be announcing our Daytona 500 plans for 2027 so early in the season,” said Long. “This is the earliest we have ever been able to plan ahead. Having Protection Technologies on board for the season opener is a testament to what Garage 66 is building, without having a charter. We have our show car on display in Orlando tonight and have the potential to carry it to other events over the winter.”

“We have the very talented Josh Bilicki lined up to get behind the wheel. I am so pleased to have the time to prepare the best car we can put together.”

“Garage 66 fans should know we have other drivers in our camp also working on Daytona 500 sponsorship, so there is the possibility Garage 66 enters more than one car. Josh could have a teammate!”

AutoRacing

The Duel at Daytona, the twin qualifying races that set the Daytona 500 starting field, is scheduled for Thursday night, February 18, 2027. The 69th Daytona 500 at Daytona International Speedway is scheduled for Sunday, February 21, 2027, live on FOX.

Ryan Preece was immune to pressure in dramatic Daytona win

by NASCAR Wire Service
August 31, 2026
Reading Time: 4 mins read
0

#60: Ryan Preece, RFK Racing, Kroger / OIKOS Ford Mustang celebrates his win

In retrospect, Tom Cruise’s presence at the Daytona International Speedway drivers’ meeting couldn’t have been more appropriate.

Cruise, who played upstart driver Cole Trickle in the 1990 film “Days of Thunder,” was there to announce that the long-awaited sequel would become reality in 2028.

The story of the race that followed the meeting read like a movie script—and an improbable one at that.

Sports News
Autos & Vehicles

Ultimately, Ryan Preece won the Coke Zero Sugar 400 to claim the final spot in the NASCAR Cup Series Chase, and next Sunday at Darlington Raceway he’ll begin his pursuit of the championship in a 100-point hole to top seed Denny Hamlin.

RELATED POSTS

2026 NASCAR Chase Preview: Denny Hamlin, Tyler Reddick and More

Goodyear Racing Notes – Darlington Raceway

Fleetio Expands 23XI Racing Deal, Continues Sponsorship of Corey Heim

Preece is used to the crucible of high-pressure moments. In 2017, he borrowed money to buy the best ride he could find for a NASCAR O’Reilly Series race at Iowa Speedway.

To use a golf analogy coined by Lee Trevino, Preece’s gamble was like playing a five-dollar Nassau with 50 cents in your pocket.

But in the No. 20 Joe Gibbs Racing Toyota, Preece won that race from the pole in a victory that launched his career into the highest echelons of stock car racing.

Before Saturday night’s Cup Series race, the 35-year-old modified driver from Berlin, Connecticut, seemed outwardly calm. He was first to the drivers’ meeting, appearing relaxed and self-assured.

Earlier, Preece had bounced into the Daytona media center to pay off a pledge he and RFK Racing team owner/driver Brad Keselowski had made to the NASCAR Foundation, one that involved dunking The Athletic journalists Jeff Gluck and Jordan Bianchi.

The driver of the No. 60 RFK Ford certainly didn’t seem like a man overwhelmed by the prospect of winning his first Cup Series points race after failing to do so in his previous 248 tries.

Preece entered the event 31 points behind Trackhouse Racing’s Shane van Gisbergen in the battle for the final Chase spot. Nearing the end of the first stage, the race took an ugly turn for the New Englander.

Running near the front of the field, Preece was collected in a three-car accident also involving teammate Chris Buescher and Kyle Larson and sustained damage to the left-front corner of his Mustang.

To make matters worse, van Gisbergen won the stage for a net of seven points over Preece, who slid across the finish line in eighth place.

The real drama, however, was reserved for overtime. By then, Preece could advance to the Chase only by winning the race, and on the final lap, he pulled ahead of Zane Smith and Tyler Reddick as a third of the field wrecked behind him.

Preece was a car-length ahead of Daniel Suarez when NASCAR called the fourth caution of the night and froze the field—and made a first-time winner of Preece.

Preece celebrated in Victory Lane with his family and his dog.

“To be able to bring my kids to Victory Lane and my wife to Victory Lane,” an emotional Preece said after the race. “(Wife) Heather has been there from when I was broke and trying to win a Stafford (Speedway) race on a Friday night so I can get my 25 percent and make $400, to her not knowing that I borrowed money and I had to pay it back somehow, to using her credit card to go get shoes at Iowa because I forgot my shoes and they were wore out that time in 2017, to moving down to North Carolina away from her friends and away from her family to chase a dream with me.

“Man, this is what racers dream of. It wasn’t given. It was earned. A lot of risk involved and I’m damn proud to be doing it with (team co-owners) Mr. Jack Roush, Brad Keselowski and the Fenway Group at RFK, and with Ford.”

Typically, the drama involving the last qualifiers for the Chase dissipates when the actual race for the championship begins. In former Chase years (before 2014), those who barely made the postseason generally were quick to fall behind.

Preece could be the exception, even with a deficit of 100 points to start the Chase.

“We started off consistent,” he said of the 2026 season. “We had a bit of a slump there in May and June, and we sort of found our way over the past few weeks, especially last week.

“We were a contender at Loudon. We were a contender tonight. Denny (Hamlin) and those guys have been really fast, but it would be great to go on one hell of a run.”
